pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ReportFindings

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

## claude-artifacts
Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. 17	## Summary
18	
19	Boarding & Salvage is the sortie: the rules that compose Interaction, Suit & Equipment, Modular Ship Assembly, Derelict Authoring and the Item & Module Database into the game's five-minute loop of entering a dark derelict, reading it by one's own light, cutting one module free, carrying it home slower than one came under a rising Attention, and seating it in the home ship. It registers no state, hook, command, mutator, read view or registry constant; it owns the order and cost of the steps, the carry-admitted set, the pod-hop cargo rule, the field-check procedure, the retreat and abandon rules, the stub-capping policy and the content-side sortie constraints. The player feels it as a held breath: read the wreck, spend light, noise and air on one take that cannot be put back, and carry it home with the dark leaning in. It serves P3 and P5 (primary), P1 (as a constraint), and P4 and P2.
20	
21	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Feature` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Interaction System (Designed), Suit & Equipment (Designed), Modular Ship Assembly (Designed), Derelict Authoring (Handmade Kits) (Designed), Item & Module Database (Designed)`; indirect: Player Controller, Life-Support Graph, Attention, Web Map & Transit (Designed); Perception Filter, Adaptive Audio & Tells, HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments, Chart Table and Debug Overlay (all Designed as of 2026-10-27; counterpart rows PF:550, AA:262, HS-43, IW:505, CT-33) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the contracts with systems still undesigned (Onboarding, Procedural Derelict Generation, Depth Rings, Knowledge Codex, Failure Contract, Co-op) are provisional
22	
23	## Overview
24	
25	Boarding & Salvage is the **sortie**: the rules that compose the game's other systems into the five-minute loop of the concept (Core Loop: fly the pod to a derelict, board it, find one salvageable system, extract it under rising Attention, return, weld or install it). It is a **composition system with zero runtime footprint**: it registers no state block, no step hook, no command type, no mutator, no read view, no notification and no registry constant (BS-1). Every verb in the index wording already has a designed owner (the pod hop, the lit act gate, the cut and cap channels, `pickup` and `drop`, the carried instance, the install, the Attention push); this GDD owns only what none of them owns: the **order and cost of the steps** as a design (the sortie sequence), the **carry-admitted set** that lets the haul reach home, the **pod-hop cargo rule**, the **field-check procedure** for suspect salvage, the **retreat and abandon rules** that make restraint a strategy, the **stub-capping policy**, the **severed-stub art direction**, the content-side sortie constraints it cites from Derelict Authoring, a set of design-time formulas, the Visual/Audio and Game Feel direction of the boarding rhythm, and the acceptance that proves a scripted sortie runs end to end. It is the one system where the player *spends*: light, noise, air, time and a take that cannot be put back.
26	
27	**How the player meets it.** They never meet a "salvage screen"; they meet a dark dock and a held breath. They ride the pod to a wreck, arrive in their own chest-lamp beam only, and **stand still** (listening is a stance, not a verb: an idle actor pushes no noise, and the Graph's hiss, creak and whistle, Attention's floor-gated hull-settling creaks (AT-26) and, once a tell opens, its structure-borne tell bed (AT-15, AUD-4) are all there is to hear). They light the room they intend to work in, **read the world** (a dried frost fan at a lagged elbow, a dead lantern, dust in the cone, the stub a given module would leave) and **decide** which one thing is worth its noise, with no value tag, rating or condition bar anywhere in the game. They cut the module free with a four-second lit channel that ends in a loud report the web hears, optionally cap the severed stubs that hiss from their own cut, lift the yield with hands that are now full, and **carry it home** at a third of a run's speed, every other prompt in the world gone but `G . Drop` until the pod console, a fitting hardpoint or a door face offers its one press *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. A tell may open on the way: they keep walking, or set the module down and run, and either is legal. They press the pod console with the module still in their arms, ride the hush home, and seat it in the vacant hardpoint, where it works and, because they put it there, costs them something new. The player finishes a sortie able to point at a module at home and say where it came from and what it cost.
28	
29	**What the game loses without it.** The concept's MVP hypothesis (the boarding-to-breach two-rhythm loop is tense and absorbing for a 30+ minute solo session) would have a breach rhythm and a life-support graph but no sortie to be tense *about*; the weld and the install would have nothing to install; the field-check ladder of Pillar 4 would have no moment at which it is run; and "retreat and restraint are real strategies" would be a slogan with no declared conditions. Without it there is no sortie.
30	
31	**Index wording reconciled.** The index (Systems Enumeration 15; Recommended Design Order 20) reads: "The boarding rhythm: enter, listen, light, decide, cut a module free, carry it home under rising Attention; field checks for suspect salvage." This GDD adopts that wording as the **shape** of the sequence and adjusts three words. (1) *Rhythm* is not a Boarding mechanic: the boarding, tell and breach rhythms are the art bible's (ART 2.6 to 2.8) and Attention's, and Boarding contributes to them only through costs the player chooses to pay (see Game Feel). (2) *Cut a module free* and *carry it home* are Interaction's verbs and the Controller's gait; Boarding states how the loop **uses** them, never how they work. (3) *Spawn* is not used for derelict A (Derelict Authoring DA-2 forbids it): A is *boarded*, *reached* or *found*. The Life-Support Graph's LS-26 and the index still say "spawn" for A; the wording refresh is routed in Cross-References, not edited.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

It is a **composition system with zero runtime footprint**: it registers no state block, no step hook, no command type, no mutator, no read view, no notification and no registry constant (BS-1). An abandoned module persists in `loose[]` as left and the derelict persists as left (WM-24, WM-28, IA-28); dropped in the dark it cannot be re-taken until something lights it (IA-28). **There is no forced drop, no hop refusal with cargo, and no tool kills a horror**: nothing is a weapon (anti-pillar), and the MVP kit has no repel tool (`tool_suppressant` is removed, user ruling X6 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the HE-39 repel stays a dormant [CUT-FIRST] interface). A horror met during a carry is answered by retreat, stillness, darkness or 'drop the cargo', which the user confirmed as the intended price of hauling (D63: Horror's figures have a carrier who keeps the cargo struck on 7 of 18 draws, with `R_SNAP_PX` 48 the lever); Horror places nothing in salvage and has no edge to author (HE:376, Designed). Every sortie step from the cut to the hop (steps 8 to 12) therefore has a legal exit. *Why.* A carried module that cannot be abandoned would turn a tell into a sentence. *Pillar.* P2, P3; anti-pillar (not a combat game). *Decided.* run rulings R13, R25. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Gating note (ruled; numbers pending).** The conditions are legal as written, and the decision they serve (keep walking, or set it down) is made live by the ruling of OQ-BS-27 (option B: the carry-state intake plus the lengthened carry, D.2 and D.3). It is live in kind (the tell opens inside the carry, holding cargo never outwaits it, and a drop does) and thin in margin: Attention's recalibration is run (F-26) and leaves a live share of 140 permille of the tell draw at 28 tiles, none at 21 to 24, and 66 to 140 permille over the lit pre-lift dwell sweep (D.2, D.3); the pass line is the boarding spike's (AC-BS-132, delegated ruling R5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*. **The stake of walking on** (named so that the choice is read and not learned as a clock) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: a walker whose drawn tell is shorter than the carry ahead arrives after `breach_due_T` and takes the breach (STRESS on the locus body, the beacon, the web's attention at the rim), a walker who arrives first voids it at no cost (AT-22), and the draw is never shown (P1); at the placeholders walking on wins in about 86 percent of draws at the reference carry, which Attention measures (AC-AT-134); OQ-AT-36 is decided (leave it, measured; delegated ruling R21, 2026-10-28) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. **Precondition (re-review)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the legal-exit claim of this rule assumes that a horror does not path or block `a_spine`, the single 3-wide corridor of the lengthened carry, at the MVP; Derelict Authoring and Horror are asked to state it (ASK-BS-H1, OQ-BS-33; request filed 2026-10-28), and if a horror may block the spine a bypass or a wider spine is required before the claim holds. No story is opened for BS-13's decision-bearing rows or for the tell acceptance rows that need a sortie-produced tell (AC-BS-72, AC-BS-122, AC-BS-123, the crossing clause of AC-BS-14b) until AC-BS-123 passes on the regenerated `REF_GOLDEN`. The fixture-armed mechanics rows (AC-BS-17, 18, 34, 35, 87, 93) test Attention's and Web Map's owned behaviour with `attention_arm_tell` and stay open as contract tests.
======
**BS-20 — Content-side sortie constraints are citations; one design target.** *Rule.* These Derelict Authoring bounds are lint-backed facts Boarding relies on and re-checks across **all five loaded sets** S0 to S4 and both sortie orders (never only the first sortie): a carried round trip to the farthest salvage through an unbreathable stretch inside Suit's vacuum budget `VACUUM_BUDGET_S` 27 s (22 tiles each way walking out and carrying back, 34 carried both ways; AC-SE-75a); A has no unbreathable stretch, so it binds B only *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, Suit R6 pod derivation)*; a hazard crossing of at most 7 tiles of lethal cold (5.6 s); `ESCAPE_ROUTE_BUDGET_PX` 1800, 600 when carrying (the endogenous-fault escape bound, DA-29, a different question from the module-saving bound); 18 / 22 module nodes (A / B); four loose parts *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the loose ledger (DA-28, DA-29, DA-21, DA-25, DA-26, DA-32). **Design target, not a lint and not registered:** a first sortie to A completes cut and carry-home in about five minutes of *player time* (concept Core Loop; measured as W_LOOP, home console press to install, with its median W_ABOARD part kept below Sanity's stage-1 point, D.1 and D.8; a long sortie that enters stage 1 is intended: Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D73 part (c) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* with `RESERVE_S` [PLACEHOLDER] and `CELL_S` [PLACEHOLDER] sufficient. The route itself is a minute-scale lower bound; the five minutes are listening, lighting, deciding and door choices, so nobody tunes the route up to hit five minutes by distance (`V_CARRY` is locked). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20) (D73): the concept's five-minute W_LOOP is kept and content is budgeted for about 200 s of discretionary dwell (D.1). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **One target:** W_LOOP (home console press to install) is the single five-minute target and every other figure derives from it: the W_ABOARD target is W_LOOP less the non-interactive pod legs and the home leg, about 259 s at the defaults (Tuning Knobs, Design targets), and the 300 s figure of D.8 and the 5-minute top of the X-BS-1 band are the stage-1 ceiling on the median, not second targets. The ruled decision carry of about 21 to 28 tiles (X3) lies with at most 7 tiles (336 px) of it inside `a_machine` (the lethal-cold cap, DA-28; DA-48 measures the carry from the cut point and its proposal puts 228 px there) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* and inside Suit's vacuum budget `VACUUM_BUDGET_S` 27 s (22 tiles each way walking out and carrying back, 34 carried both ways; AC-SE-75a); A has no unbreathable stretch, so it binds B only *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, Suit R6 pod derivation)*; whether a 1008 to 1344 px carried leg passes `ESCAPE_ROUTE_BUDGET_PX` 600 when carrying (DA-29, a different question from the module-saving bound) is Derelict Authoring's lint question (OQ-BS-31). This GDD's reading: the 600 px bound is the endogenous-fault escape bound and does not apply to a non-fault decision carry; if Derelict Authoring's lint applies it to every carried leg, the ruled decision carry needs an explicit exemption, or the lint rejects the ruled route (ASK-BS-D4 (e), AC-BS-52) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Sanity's dwell cost is cited and not set: `ABOARD_EXPOSURE` [PLACEHOLDER] (SN). **Subject budget:** Boarding adds no subject beyond the drops `P <= PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE` and forbids any rule here that seeds more loose items; the post-weld sortie S4 `{home+B, A}` already exceeds `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` by 24 (144 vs 120, DA OQ-DA-20, owned by Derelict Authoring and Interaction, C-BS-7). Node anchors are not published by Derelict Authoring, so every route figure in this GDD is marked as assumed and deferred to Layout's `route_length_px` (ASK-BS-D1). *Why.* The authored bounds are what keep a carried return survivable and a retreat legal across every loaded set; citing them and minting no lint of Boarding's own keeps Derelict Authoring the one owner of the geometry, while the design target names only the felt length. *Pillar.* P2, P5. *Decided.* run rulings R23, R24, R29.

content.content:
### D.4 `hazard_dwell_budget`

The hazard_dwell_budget formula is defined as:

`dwell = ceil(px_in / V_WALK) + T_open + n_cuts * SALVAGE_CHANNEL_TICKS + T_scan + px_out / V_CARRY` ; `margin_pm = floor(1000 * dwell / T_crit)` ; for the unbreathable branch `traverse_runs = ceil(round_trip_ticks / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)` ; `reserve_cost_mgu = traverse_runs * R_BREATH` ; `reserve_left_mgu = max(0, arrival_reserve - reserve_cost_mgu)` ; `reserve_pm = floor(1000 * reserve_cost_mgu / arrival_reserve)` with the guard `arrival_reserve = 0 -> reserve_pm = 1000, everything unserved` (G5; boundary AC in AC-BS-106) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, Suit R6 pod derivation)* (the former `reserve_pm` over `RESERVE_S * TICK_RATE`, 497 at 56 tiles, is deleted except as a label: the share of a FULL reserve, the stale reading) ; `T_crit` is DA D.10's `runs_critical * GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` (cited, not re-derived)

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `px_in`, `px_out` | int px | up to 7 tiles x 48 = 336 inside the cold room | DA-28 (the crossing bound); `[ASSUMED anchor]` 204 px | the in-room legs, walked in and carried out |
| `T_open` | int ticks | 0 or 30 | Interaction IA-24 (`DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER]) | opening `door_a_spine_machine` from outside costs no cold; count 0 if the sill is not crossed |
| `n_cuts` | int | 1 to 8 | the player | cuts made in one visit |
| `T_scan` | int ticks | 0 or 120 | Interaction (`FIELD_CHECK_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER]) | a SCAN taken inside |
| `T_crit` | int ticks | 2184 (364 runs, CRITICAL at `T0` -22000 mC); FAILED at 6546 (1091 runs) | DA D.10 / Suit D.4 | the cold clock at the room's authored temperature |
| `round_trip_ticks` | int ticks | up to 1,632 (34 tiles carried both ways = Suit's `VACUUM_BUDGET_RUNS` after two legs; DA D.7 conformed, see the DA request); the former 2,688 (56 tiles) is withdrawn *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, Suit R6 pod derivation)* | Suit D.11 / AC-SE-75a (DA-28 and D.7 conform) | a carried round trip through an unbreathable stretch |
| `RESERVE_S` | int s | 90 (45 to 240) [PLACEHOLDER] | Suit | the engaged reserve breath; the reserve at the airlock is `RESERVE_S` x 3000 mGU less the outbound pod leg *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, Suit R6 pod derivation)* |
| `arrival_reserve` | int mGU | [222,600, 222,900] at the defaults ([221,100, 221,400] on the 975-tick slack leg) | Suit D.1 'Pod leg derivation' (QUOTED, NOT re-derived): `max(0, RESERVE_MAX_MGU 270,000 - d x N)` with d = `R_BREATH` 300 mGU per run, N = 158 / 157 runs on the nominal 945-tick leg, 47,100 to 47,400 mGU = 17.4 percent | the reserve at the airlock; it drains in the pod because the statuses run there (D60, R6) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, Suit R6 pod derivation)* |
| `R_BREATH` | int mGU per run | 300 | Suit | the reserve spent per 6-tick run while breath_src is RESERVE |
| `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` | int ticks | 6 | Life-Support Graph | ticks per run |
| `RESERVE_WARN_MGU` | int mGU | 90,000 | Suit | the warn edge (`RESERVE_WARN_S` 30 s x 3000) |

**Output Range:** `dwell` from `SALVAGE_CHANNEL_TICKS` (240, a cut with no crossing) to `dwell_fixed + n_cuts * SALVAGE_CHANNEL_TICKS` (2226 for eight cuts at the defaults, where `dwell_fixed` = 306 = 102 + 0 + 204 without a SCAN); `margin_pm` above 1000 means CRITICAL is reached. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, Suit R6 pod derivation)*: `reserve_pm` is 1000 with everything unserved for `arrival_reserve` 0 (the guard; the Suit range floor of `RESERVE_S` 45 cannot make the arrival reserve 0 on a nominal leg, but a long leg, a low reserve or an injected route can) and `T_crit` must be positive (DA D.10 guarantees it). A route with `margin_pm >= 1000` for its authored crossing is a Derelict Authoring lint failure, not a Boarding rule. The Graph's room cools and the gain rises over a long visit, so these margins shrink; they are exact only at `T0`.

**Example:** `htr_a` with the assumed anchors: `102 + 0 + 240 + 0 + 204` = **546 ticks = 9.1 s = 250 permille** of `T_crit` 2184. With one SCAN: 666 (30 percent). Worst case inside DA's 7-tile bound with a SCAN: `168 + 0 + 240 + 120 + 336` = **864 ticks = 14.4 s = 395 permille** (`floor(1000 * 864 / 2184)`), leaving 1320 ticks (22 s). Each further cut in the visit adds 240: `dwell(n) = 306 + 240 n` gives 1026 (47 percent) for three, 1506 (69 percent) for five, 1986 (91 percent) for seven, and **2226 for eight, which exceeds 2184**: `a_machine` holds about eight module nodes (DA C.2), so stripping the room is lethal by construction; it tolerates one purposeful cut and a shuttle, not a strip. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *("eight cuts" holds only at the default `T_crit` 2184 and `SALVAGE_CHANNEL_TICKS` 240. As a function of the live constants the lethal count is `n_lethal = floor((T_crit - dwell_fixed) / SALVAGE_CHANNEL_TICKS) + 1`, which is 8 at the defaults (`floor((2184 - 306) / 240) + 1`) and moves with `A_MACHINE_T_MC`, `SALVAGE_CHANNEL_TICKS` and the anchors. The statement "stripping `a_machine` is lethal" is therefore a lint on Derelict Authoring's side, `module_nodes(a_machine) >= n_lethal`, and not a constant of this GDD.)* The irony is the authored one (DA-28): `htr_a` is the heater that keeps `a_machine` survivable once the bus is woken, so cutting it removes the thing that would have made lingering safe.

### D.10 `lamp_cell_budget`

The lamp_cell_budget formula is defined as:

`cell_share_pm = min(1000, floor(1000 * lit_ticks / (CELL_S * TICK_RATE)))` ; `sorties_per_cell = floor(CELL_S * TICK_RATE / lit_ticks)` for `lit_ticks >= 1`, and the sentinel `UNBOUNDED` for `lit_ticks = 0` (a dark sortie spends no cell, so the quotient does not exist) ; `sorties_to_empty = ceil(CELL_S * TICK_RATE / lit_ticks)` at a constant lit cost per sortie and no refill between sorties (the sortie in which the cell reaches 0) ; with the ruled `top_up`: `cell_after_refill = min(CELL_S * TICK_RATE, cell_left + refill_ticks)`, where `refill_ticks` is the credit of one lit bare-hand TAP at a home BATTERY port, never more than the deficit (Suit D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(the `lit_ticks = 0` guard and the clamp are the review's; `sorties_to_strand` is renamed `sorties_to_empty` because an empty cell no longer strands, BS-19; the refill term is Suit's, cited and not defined here)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lit_ticks` | int ticks | 0 to `T_SORTIE_SAFE_TICKS` 28,800 for a safe sortie (a lit sortie may run longer; the clamp covers it); realistic play 1,278 (the reference line) to 18,000 (a 300 s survey) | the player's beam use (`toggle_beam`, SE-8 to SE-10) | ticks with the chest lamp on while aboard and, because the statuses run in the pod (user ruling D60), ticks with the lamp left on during a hop, counted as 6 ticks per lit run (the statuses run in the pod, D60, R6): a nominal 945-tick leg holds 157 or 158 runs, so a fully lit leg debits 942 (N_lo) to 948 (N_hi) lit ticks, up to 978 on the 975-tick slack leg (163 runs); Suit drains GRAPH_STEP_TICKS per lit run (SE-8), Web Map WM-17 conforms *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
| `CELL_S` | int s | 1200 (600 to 2400) [PLACEHOLDER] | Suit | seconds of lit beam in a full cell; 72,000 ticks at the default |
| `RESERVE_S` | int s | 90 (45 to 240) [PLACEHOLDER] | Suit | engaged reserve breath, spent in an unbreathable stretch AND in the pod (the pod cabin is ANOXIC, Suit D.1 pod derivation), 47,100 to 47,400 mGU per nominal leg (D.4) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
| `GLOWSTICK_START_COUNT` | int | 2 (0 to 4) [PLACEHOLDER] | Suit | sticks in the start kit; each lights 150 s (`GLOWSTICK_LIFE_S` [PLACEHOLDER]) |
| `refill_ticks` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | int ticks | 0 to the deficit, per `top_up` TAP | Suit D.9 (`cell_deficit_ticks`, `CELL_STOCK_PER_KTICK` [PH]) | the cell credited by one lit bare-hand `top_up` at a home BATTERY port; the stock it withdraws is the home battery's (a store, not a power draw, so invisible to Attention) |

**Output Range:** `cell_share_pm` 0 to 1000 (clamped), and 17 to 400 over the realistic and safe-sortie `lit_ticks` above. `sorties_per_cell` is `UNBOUNDED` at `lit_ticks` 0, **56 at the reference line** (28 to 112 across `CELL_S` 600 to 2400), 4 at the 300 s survey and 2 at the 28,800-tick safe-sortie bound. The earlier range "1 to about 56" and the earlier `lit_ticks` bound of 18,000 were wrong at both ends.

**Example (FIXTURE-312, the 13-tile pre-ruling schedule; see D.2 fixture convention):** the reference line from arrival to the console with the beam on throughout: `312 + 60 + 240 + 12 + 624 + 30` = 1278 ticks (the 12 is the pickup dwell and the 30 the console approach, both fixture dwells of the D.2 golden schedule) = 21.3 s: `floor(1000 * 1278 / 72000)` = **17 permille** of `CELL_S`, `floor(72000 / 1278)` = 56 sorties. A survey sortie lit for 300 s (18,000 ticks) is **250 permille**: `sorties_per_cell` 4 and `sorties_to_empty` 4. *Built-route reading (indicative, the ruled 28-tile route, D.1):* `672 + 60 + 240 + 12 + 1,344 + 30` = 2,358 lit ticks = 39.3 s, 32 permille, 30 sorties. **Beam left lit across both nominal pod legs** adds 1,884 to 1,896 ticks (2.6 percent of `CELL_S`): the fixture reference line 1,278 becomes 3,162 to 3,174 (`cell_share_pm` 43 to 44, `sorties_per_cell` 22) and a 300 s survey 18,000 becomes 19,884 to 19,896 (276 permille, `sorties_per_cell` 3, `sorties_to_empty` 4). The default expectation is beam off in the pod (Suit AC-SE-36a runs with the beam off); the lit-leg cost is the player's choice *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Each stick thrown aboard adds 180 AU raw (`U_LOUD` [PLACEHOLDER]) to D.2's intake. A 30-minute session of two derelict sorties in the survey style spends about half the cell; the MVP refill is V7 `top_up` at a lit home BATTERY port (user ruling X5, D70b) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **Campaign reading** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: a lit-beam player who surveys at 300 s per sortie empties the cell in about four sorties **between refills**, and then chooses between refilling at home with `top_up`, going dark deliberately, or spending sticks (the authored sticks of the A route, 2 + 2 + 4 = 8, each 150 s, B's shelves not counted). No choice strands them, because the dock console is lit by the pod's status glow whatever the cell (BS-19). The dark-dock strand is therefore no longer a campaign-length event; AC-BS-92 still runs on the campaign-length strand cell, now to prove that the glow holds the invariant. Lighting less (a deliberate dark walk with `toggle_beam`) saves cell and costs sight of the frost sill. *Design-time; the home ship's lamps are fixtures, not the chest lamp.*

content.content:
### States and Transitions

**Boarding & Salvage has no stored state** (BS-1). The template requires a state table, so the table below is a **fixture and design vocabulary**: each label is a predicate over fields the owners already hold, computed and never written, never registered, never persisted, and never a name in any file, command or event. It exists so that the headless reference sortie (Acceptance Criteria) and the Game Feel arc can nam

**The four owner axes the labels read** (nothing else is consulted):

| Axis | Owner field | Values used |
|---|---|---|
| Where | `body_of_actor` / `actor_section` (BDY); `transit_state` (WM) | home body; derelict locus body; in transit (`IDLE`, `LEG`, `ARRIVING`, `BERTHING`) |
| What the hands do | `controller.state.loco_state` (PC) and `channel_ref` | `IDLE`, `WALK`, `RUN`, `CARRY_WALK`, `CHANNELLING`, `STAGGERED`, `DOWNED`, `IN_POD` |
| What is held | `controller.state.carry_ref` (PC-8), cross-checked with `suit.state.carried_id` (SE-13) | none / one carried instance |
| What the web is doing | Attention `phase` (AT) | `CALM`, `TELL`, `BREACH`, `SUBSIDING` |

**Labels (derived, never stored):**

| Label | Derived from | Entry | Exit | Legal transitions | Who may cause them |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HOME | actor in the home body; `transit_state` `IDLE` | boot, or arrival from a hop | `pod_hop` Applied | to TRANSIT_OUT | the player (`pod_hop`, WM-8) |
| TRANSIT_OUT | `transit_state` `LEG` with origin home; `loco_state` `IN_POD` | `pod_hop` Applied (a body transfer; aborts any channel, IA-40) | `pod_arrive` / `pod_settle` after `HOP_LEG_TICKS` and `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` | to ABOARD_QUIET | Web Map's machine (WM-14); the player only by pressing the console |
| ABOARD_QUIET | actor in a derelict locus body; no `channel_ref`; hands free or a tool in hand; `phase` not `TELL`/`BREACH` | arrival; a channel ends or aborts; `drop` | a channel begins; `pickup`; a TELL opens | to ABOARD_JOB, LOADED, ABOARD_TELL | the player (verbs); Attention (phase) |
| ABOARD_JOB | `loco_state` `CHANNELLING` on `begin_cut`, `begin_cap` or `field_check` | channel `Applied` (lit, in reach) | completion; abort (IA-15: MOVED, CANCELLED, UNLIT, OUT_OF_REACH, TARGET_GONE, BODY, NOT_ELIGIBLE, RESTORE); a TELL opens (the channel is not aborted by it) | to ABOARD_QUIET, ABOARD_TELL | the player; the abort set; Attention (phase) |
| LOADED | `carry_ref` set; `loco_state` `CARRY_WALK` or `IDLE` | `pickup` Applied (IA-28) | `drop`; downed (PC-9); `install_module`; `pod_hop` carries it across (state persists) | to ABOARD_QUIET (drop), HOME (via hop), INSTALLED | the player; Suit's limiter via PC-9 (downed) |
| ABOARD_TELL | `phase` `TELL` and the actor in the locus body | Attention enters TELL (AT-8) | abort by stillness (AT-10), breach due, or departure | to ABOARD_QUIET (abort), ABOARD_BREACH, TRANSIT_BACK | Attention only; the player's restraint or departure shapes it |
| ABOARD_BREACH | `phase` `BREACH` or `SUBSIDING`, actor in `locus_body` (AT-15) | tell expiry | the last recorded occupant leaves a non-home locus body (AT-22) | to TRANSIT_BACK | Attention (the harm), the player (departure) |
| TRANSIT_BACK | `transit_state` `LEG` with origin a derelict; `loco_state` `IN_POD` | `pod_hop` Applied from a dock room (always allowed, WM-26) | arrival at home | to HOME (and still LOADED if `carry_ref` is set) | the player; Web Map's machine |
| INSTALLED | M5 `install_module` Applied (MSA-26) | the module seated in a hardpoint | **terminal for that module** (no `remove_module`, MSA-28; V8 salvage is the only way out) | none | the player (`install_module`) |
| DOWNED | `loco_state` `DOWNED` (Suit limiter FAILED, SE-24) | the limiter reaches FAILED | revive (VS-B); the solo give-up-and-reload action (user ruling D7 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*); `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` elapses, then DEAD, then restore from the newest autosave (SL-7) | to ABOARD_QUIET (revive), restore | Suit/Controller (the limiter); the host (restore) |

**Transition rules worth stating once.**

1. **LOADED is an overlay, not a place.** It combines with every aboard label (a tell during a carry is ABOARD_TELL and LOADED at once); the fixture reports both.
2. **Any aboard label may go to TRANSIT_BACK from any dock room with the pod docked there, whatever the cargo** (WM-26, WM:414 envelope). If the console row is refused (C-BS-1), a LOADED actor must first `drop` and the module stays aboard (Edge Cases).
